title: Which Line Has Moved?
endLine: To read a sick heart, ask which line has moved.

scenes.tts: Last time, each beat ended where two lines crossed: the ventricle's line and the arteries' line. But a loop also has a floor. When a heart fails, which line has moved?
scenes.narration: Last time, each beat ended where two lines crossed: the ventricle's line and the arteries' line. But a loop also has a floor. When a heart fails, which line has moved?
scenes.caption: Last time, each beat ended where two lines crossed: the ventricle's line and the arteries' line. But a loop also has a floor. When a heart fails, which line has moved?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset. One plot fills about 70% of the frame height: y axis 'pressure (mmHg)', 0 to 160; x axis 'volume (mL)', 0 to 250. The model baseline loop from the first film, computed: corners at 125 mL and 10 mmHg (mitral closes), 125 mL and 80 mmHg (aortic opens), 45 mL and 120 mmHg (aortic closes), 45 mL and about 5 mmHg (mitral opens); a WHITE dot runs round it counterclockwise throughout the film. GREEN ventricle's line: pressure = 3.0 x (volume - 5), drawn from 5 mL up to about 55 mL. ORANGE arteries' line: pressure = 1.5 x (125 - volume), from 125 mL on the axis up to the top-left corner. On 'crossed', the top-left corner pulses where GREEN meets ORANGE. On 'a floor', the loop's bottom edge glows CYAN. On the question, the baseline loop dims to a dashed WHITE ghost labelled 'normal', and two MAGENTA question-mark loops flicker beside it, one far to the right and one with a raised floor (schematic). White text across the top: 'Which line has moved?'

Title 'Which Line Has Moved?' fades in above the plot for 2 s while the question text and the two MAGENTA question-mark loops fade out. The baseline loop returns to full WHITE; the dot keeps circling; GREEN and ORANGE lines stay.

scenes.tts: Under the loop runs a third line, a soft curve. It is the passive filling curve, the end diastolic pressure volume relation. Once relaxation is complete, the bottom of the loop lies on it. Its slope indexes chamber stiffness.
scenes.narration: Under the loop runs a third line, a soft curve. It is the passive filling curve, the end-diastolic pressure-volume relation. Once relaxation is complete, the bottom of the loop lies on it. Its slope indexes chamber stiffness.
scenes.caption: Under the loop runs a third line, a soft curve. It is the passive filling curve, the end-diastolic pressure-volume relation. Once relaxation is complete, the bottom of the loop lies on it. Its slope indexes chamber stiffness.
scenes.visual: The CYAN glow on the loop's floor extends into a full curve, low and nearly flat at small volumes, bending upward to the right; it passes under the loop's bottom edge and meets the bottom-right corner near 125 mL and 10 mmHg. Shape is schematic: tag 'schematic' beneath it. Label 'filling curve'. On 'bottom of the loop lies on it', the WHITE dot slides along the loop's floor, riding on the CYAN curve. On 'slope', a small CYAN tangent wedge appears near the bottom-right corner, labelled 'stiffness'. Now three lines on screen: GREEN, ORANGE, CYAN.

scenes.tts: Start with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Remodelling shifts the ventricle's line, the floor and the loop to the right. The ventricle's line is usually flatter, its contractility index lower. The result is a large chamber ejecting a small fraction of its volume.
scenes.narration: Start with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Remodelling shifts the ventricle's line, the floor and the loop to the right. The ventricle's line is usually flatter, its contractility index lower. The result is a large chamber ejecting a small fraction of its volume.
scenes.caption: Start with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Remodelling shifts the ventricle's line, the floor and the loop to the right. The ventricle's line is usually flatter, its contractility index lower. The result is a large chamber ejecting a small fraction of its volume.
scenes.visual: Tag top left: 'reduced EF'. The baseline loop stays as a dashed WHITE ghost labelled 'normal'. Schematic, no numbers on the new shapes: the GREEN line, the CYAN curve and the loop all slide right together toward 150 to 220 mL; then the GREEN line pivots flatter. The loop becomes MAGENTA: shifted to large volumes with a short top edge, far right of the ghost. On 'small fraction', a YELLOW stroke-volume arrow under the MAGENTA loop stays short while a pale bar spans the chamber's full volume from the axis, showing a small share ejected. The ORANGE line follows the new end-diastolic volume. Tag 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: So ask of every sick loop, not only how much it ejects, but which line has moved. The ventricle's line tracks the squeeze. The floor tracks filling. The arteries' line tracks the load.
scenes.narration: So ask of every sick loop, not only how much it ejects, but which line has moved. The ventricle's line tracks the squeeze. The floor tracks filling. The arteries' line tracks the load.
scenes.caption: So ask of every sick loop, not only how much it ejects, but which line has moved. The ventricle's line tracks the squeeze. The floor tracks filling. The arteries' line tracks the load.
scenes.visual: The reduced-EF shapes fade; the WHITE baseline loop returns with its GREEN, ORANGE and CYAN lines. White text at top: 'Which line has moved?' On 'squeeze', the GREEN line glows and gets a label 'squeeze'; on 'filling', the CYAN curve glows, label 'filling'; on 'load', the ORANGE line glows, label 'load'. The three labels stay for the rest of the film. The dot keeps circling.

scenes.tts: Now heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Here the floor moves. Catheter studies found the filling curve shifted up and to the left. Passive stiffness was higher, and relaxation was slower.
scenes.narration: Now heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Here the floor moves. Catheter studies found the filling curve shifted up and to the left. Passive stiffness was higher, and relaxation was slower.
scenes.caption: Now heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Here the floor moves. Catheter studies found the filling curve shifted up and to the left. Passive stiffness was higher, and relaxation was slower.
scenes.visual: Tag top left: 'preserved EF'. The text 'Which line has moved?' stays. The CYAN curve leaves a faint CYAN ghost labelled 'normal floor' and slides up and to the left, bending more steeply (schematic, no numbers). On 'relaxation was slower', the WHITE dot visibly slows as it runs down the loop's left side, then resumes its pace. GREEN and ORANGE lines unchanged for now.

scenes.tts: Fill this stiffer chamber to the same volume as a normal one. What happens to the pressure at the bottom right corner, where filling ends?
scenes.narration: Fill this stiffer chamber to the same volume as a normal one. What happens to the pressure at the bottom right corner, where filling ends?
scenes.caption: Fill this stiffer chamber to the same volume as a normal one. What happens to the pressure at the bottom right corner, where filling ends?
scenes.visual: A vertical dashed WHITE line drops from the baseline end-diastolic volume, 125 mL, to the axis, labelled 'same volume'. It crosses both the faint CYAN 'normal floor' ghost and the shifted CYAN curve; the crossings are NOT marked yet. Question card at top in white: 'Same volume: what pressure?'
Predict pause. The question card 'Same volume: what pressure?' stays. The WHITE dot circles slowly; the dashed 'same volume' line and both CYAN curves hold still. No other change.

scenes.tts: It runs higher. On a floor shifted up and left, the same volume sits at a higher pressure. A catheter study of seventy people with this condition found stiffer chambers at rest. When handgrip raised afterload, their end diastolic pressures rose more than in the comparison group. The study did not show what causes the stiffness.
scenes.narration: It runs higher. On a floor shifted up and left, the same volume sits at a higher pressure. A catheter study of 70 people with this condition found stiffer chambers at rest. When handgrip raised afterload, their end-diastolic pressures rose more than in the comparison group. The study did not show what causes the stiffness.
scenes.caption: It runs higher. On a floor shifted up and left, the same volume sits at a higher pressure. A catheter study of 70 people with this condition found stiffer chambers at rest. When handgrip raised afterload, their end-diastolic pressures rose more than in the comparison group. The study did not show what causes the stiffness.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. Two dots appear where the 'same volume' line meets each CYAN curve: a low one on the 'normal floor' ghost and a higher one on the shifted curve; a vertical CYAN arrow between them, labelled 'higher filling pressure' (schematic, no number). On 'catheter study', a small card at right: 'catheter study, 70 people'. On 'handgrip', a fist icon squeezes; the ORANGE line tilts a little steeper, and the bottom-right corner of a MAGENTA loop on the shifted floor rises up its CYAN curve, further than a ghost corner on the normal floor does. The ORANGE line then returns. On 'did not show what causes', a question mark settles beside the shifted CYAN curve, labelled 'cause?'.

scenes.tts: In a small catheter study, the ventricle's line was steeper too. But that slope belongs to the whole chamber. Thick walls and passive stiffness can steepen it. In one community study, the slope was raised, yet contractility was depressed. A steeper line need not mean stronger muscle.
scenes.narration: In a small catheter study, the ventricle's line was steeper too. But that slope belongs to the whole chamber. Thick walls and passive stiffness can steepen it. In one community study, the slope was raised, yet contractility was depressed. A steeper line need not mean stronger muscle.
scenes.caption: In a small catheter study, the ventricle's line was steeper too. But that slope belongs to the whole chamber. Thick walls and passive stiffness can steepen it. In one community study, the slope was raised, yet contractility was depressed. A steeper line need not mean stronger muscle.
scenes.visual: The 'cause?' question mark stays beside the shifted CYAN curve. On 'steeper too', the GREEN line pivots steeper (dashed, schematic). On 'whole chamber', the GREEN line's 'squeeze' label splits into two small tags beside it: 'muscle' and 'walls + stiffness'. On 'thick walls', the 'walls + stiffness' tag glows. On 'community study', the 'muscle' tag dims downward while the steep GREEN line stays steep. On 'need not mean stronger muscle', the dimmed 'muscle' tag and the steep dashed GREEN line pulse once. Tag 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: In aortic stenosis, the narrowed valve adds to afterload. Ventricular pressure climbs, and the top of the loop domes upward. A thickened wall can keep ejection fraction near normal, until the ventricle starts to fail.
scenes.narration: In aortic stenosis, the narrowed valve adds to afterload. Ventricular pressure climbs, and the top of the loop domes upward. A thickened wall can keep ejection fraction near normal, until the ventricle starts to fail.
scenes.caption: In aortic stenosis, the narrowed valve adds to afterload. Ventricular pressure climbs, and the top of the loop domes upward. A thickened wall can keep ejection fraction near normal, until the ventricle starts to fail.
scenes.visual: The preserved-EF shapes fade and the WHITE baseline loop returns, the GREEN label back to 'squeeze', with GREEN, ORANGE and CYAN lines. Tag top left: 'aortic stenosis'. A small valve icon on the ORANGE line narrows to a slit. The ORANGE line tilts steeper. The loop becomes MAGENTA: its top edge bulges upward into a dome well above 120 mmHg (schematic, no number), while its bottom-right corner stays near 125 mL. On 'thickened wall', the GREEN line steepens too (schematic), so the top-left corner rises but stays near its baseline volume and the YELLOW stroke-volume arrow under the loop holds near its baseline length.

scenes.tts: Reduced ejection fraction, preserved ejection fraction, a narrowed valve: each moves different lines. Read the loop for where the trouble sits, in the squeeze, the filling or the load.
scenes.narration: Reduced ejection fraction, preserved ejection fraction, a narrowed valve: each moves different lines. Read the loop for where the trouble sits, in the squeeze, the filling or the load.
scenes.caption: Reduced ejection fraction, preserved ejection fraction, a narrowed valve: each moves different lines. Read the loop for where the trouble sits, in the squeeze, the filling or the load.
scenes.visual: The plot splits into three small copies side by side, each with a dashed WHITE 'normal' ghost loop (schematic): 'reduced EF' with its GREEN line flatter and loop shifted right; 'preserved EF' with its CYAN floor raised; 'aortic stenosis' with its ORANGE line steeper and domed top. On 'squeeze', the moved GREEN line glows in the first copy; on 'filling', the moved CYAN floor in the second; on 'load', the steeper ORANGE line in the third. WHITE dots keep circling all three loops.
End card over the dimmed but still moving three-plot world, dots circling. Large white text, centred: 'To read a sick heart, ask which line has moved.'
